name: Acute Tonsillitis / Pharyngitis (GAS / Sore Throat)
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus - GAS)
comments: Routine antibiotic treatment is NOT indicated for viral pharyngitis (majority). For proven or high-suspicion GAS (Centor/McIsaac score ≥3), complete a full 10-day course of penicillin or amoxicillin to prevent Acute Rheumatic Fever (ARF) and suppurative complications.

antibiotics.label: Penicillin V (Phenoxymethylpenicillin) PO (First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day) for 10 full days
antibiotics.notes: Take 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. Must complete full 10 days to eradicate carriage and prevent rheumatic fever.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin PO (Alternative First-Line - Better Taste & OD Dosing)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/day PO once daily (OD) or in 2 divided doses (max. 1g/day) for 10 full days
antibiotics.notes: Once-daily dosing (50mg/kg OD, max 1g/day) is endorsed by NAG 2024, AHA, and IDSA as equivalent efficacy to Penicillin V, with better adherence and suspension taste.

antibiotics.label: Benzylpenicillin (Penicillin G) IV (Severe / Inability to swallow)
antibiotics.doseText: 100,000 - 200,000 units/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 24 million units/day)
antibiotics.duration: 10 days total (switch to oral once tolerating)
antibiotics.notes: For severe cases or peritonsillar cellulitis unable to tolerate oral therapy. Switch to oral penicillin V or amoxicillin once improved.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (Non-severe Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day) for 10 days
antibiotics.notes: Safe for non-life-threatening penicillin allergy (maculopapular rash). Complete 10 days.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO (Severe Penicillin Anaphylaxis)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 800mg/dose, 2g/day) for 10 days
antibiotics.notes: Indicated for true IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to beta-lactams.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (Severe Allergy Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 12 mg/kg/day PO once daily (max. 500mg/day) for 5 days
antibiotics.notes: High tissue concentration allows shorter 5-day course.

name: Acute Otitis Media (AOM)
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, non-typeable H. influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis
comments: Watchful waiting (48-72h) recommended if ≥2 years with mild unilateral symptoms. High-dose Amoxicillin is preferred to overcome intermediate penicillin-resistant S. pneumoniae.

antibiotics.label: High-Dose Amoxicillin PO (Preferred First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 3 divided doses (max. 1g/dose, 3g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Duration: 10 days for age <2 years; 5-7 days for age ≥2 years.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate (Augmentin 7:1) (Failure at 48-72h / Conjunctivitis-Otitis)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin component) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g amoxicillin/day)
antibiotics.notes: Indicated if child received amoxicillin in past 30 days or failed to improve after 48-72 hours.

antibiotics.label: Cefuroxime Axetil PO (Non-severe Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 30 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 250mg/dose, 500mg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Take with food to increase bioavailability and mask bitter taste.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (Severe Type 1 Penicillin Anaphylaxis)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 mg/kg/day PO OD on Day 1 (max. 500mg), then 5 mg/kg/day PO OD on Days 2-5 (max. 250mg)
antibiotics.notes: Reserve for true beta-lactam anaphylaxis.

name: Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis (ABRS)
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, H. influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis
comments: Majority of rhinosinusitis is viral. Suspect bacterial when: 1. Symptoms persist ≥10 days without improvement; 2. Worsening double-sickening course; 3. High fever ≥39°C with purulent nasal discharge for ≥3 consecutive days.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin PO (Preferred First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day) for 5 days
antibiotics.notes: NAG 2024 recommends 5-day course. Re-evaluate if not improving after 72 hours.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1) (High Risk / Daycare / Prior Antibiotics)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day) for 5 days
antibiotics.notes: Covers beta-lactamase producing H. influenzae and Moraxella.

antibiotics.label: Cefuroxime Axetil PO (Non-life-threatening Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 30 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 1g/day) for 5 days
antibiotics.notes: Second-generation cephalosporin for non-IgE penicillin allergy.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO (Severe Beta-Lactam Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 800mg/dose, 2g/day) for 5 days
antibiotics.notes: For patients with true immediate anaphylaxis.

name: Acute Epiglottitis / Supraglottitis
commonOrganisms: Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), Streptococcus pyogenes, S. pneumoniae, S. aureus
comments: AIRWAY EMERGENCY! Do NOT examine throat with spatula. Transfer immediately to operating theatre with ENT and Anaesthesiology for controlled airway securing before any blood taking or invasive procedures.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Preferred First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Administer immediately after airway is secured.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 100 mg/kg/day IV once daily (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Potent parenteral broad-spectrum third generation cephalosporin.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (Add if Staph aureus / toxic shock suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Covers MSSA.

name: Respiratory Diphtheria (Updated Jan '26)
commonOrganisms: Corynebacterium diphtheriae (toxin-producing)
comments: NOTIFY IMMEDIATELY! Administer Diphtheria Antitoxin (DAT) without delay based on clinical suspicion and membrane extent. Strict respiratory isolation. Trace and treat close contacts.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO/IV (First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 4 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day) for 14 days
antibiotics.notes: Eradicates organism to halt toxin production. Complete full 14-day course. Document negative repeat swabs at 24h & 48h post-treatment.

antibiotics.label: Benzylpenicillin (Penicillin G) IV (Alternative First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 100,000 - 150,000 units/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 12 million units/day) for 14 days
antibiotics.notes: Parenteral therapy until patient can comfortably swallow oral erythromycin.

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) - Outpatient / Mild
commonOrganisms: Viral (RSV, Influenza, hMPV), Streptococcus pneumoniae, Group A Streptococcus, H. influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae
comments: Antibiotics are not routinely recommended if viral infection is suspected. For bacterial suspicion in outpatient setting, high-dose Amoxicillin is preferred. Review at 48 hours.

antibiotics.label: High-dose Amoxicillin (Preferred)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 90 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 3 divided doses (max. 1g/dose, 3g/day) for 5 days
antibiotics.notes: NAG 2024 & WHO endorse weight-band dosing to streamline prescribing and minimize calculation errors. Safe wide therapeutic index.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate (Alternative / Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 800mg/dose, 2g/day) for 7-10 days
antibiotics.notes: Indicated if Mycoplasma pneumoniae suspected, or in penicillin allergy.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin (Atypical Pathogens / Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 mg/kg/day PO OD on Day 1 (max. 500mg), then 5 mg/kg/day PO OD on Days 2-5 (max. 250mg)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once-daily dosing. Use for suspected atypical pneumonia.

name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) - Inpatient / Severe
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Group A Streptococcus, H. influenzae
comments: Obtain blood culture prior to antibiotics. Switch to oral antibiotics once child is afebrile for 24-48h and clinically improved.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (First-Line Inpatient)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred empiric parenteral therapy for fully immunized children without empyema.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Severe / Unimmunised / Pleural Effusion)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Indicated if critically ill, unimmunized, or with effusion.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Inpatient / Once Daily)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 80 mg/kg/day IV in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Avoid concurrent calcium-containing IV solutions.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (Add for MSSA / Cavitary / Pneumatocele)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Add if Staphylococcus aureus is clinically suspected.

name: Empyema Thoracis / Parapneumonic Effusion
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Group A Streptococcus
comments: Diagnostic thoracocentesis & chest drain insertion required. Continue IV antibiotics until chest tube removed and fever resolved, then switch to oral.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin/Sulbactam IV (Unasyn)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day (ampicillin component) IV in 4 divided doses (max. 8g ampicillin/day)
antibiotics.notes: Broad coverage including anaerobic and beta-lactamase producing organisms.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV PLUS Cloxacillin IV
antibiotics.doseText: Cefotaxime 150-200 mg/kg/day IV q6h + Cloxacillin 100-200 mg/kg/day IV q6h
antibiotics.notes: Covers both Gram-negative/pneumococcal pathogens and MSSA.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (If MRSA suspected or critical sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Monitor trough level.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 15-20 mcg/mL.

name: Acute Pyelonephritis / Febrile UTI (≥3 months)
commonOrganisms: Escherichia coli (80%), Klebsiella spp., Proteus mirabilis, Enterobacter spp.
comments: Obtain clean-catch or catheter urine culture prior to starting antibiotics. Duration: 7 to 10 days. Switch to oral once afebrile for 48h.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (First Line Oral)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: First-line oral option for mild to moderate pyelonephritis tolerating fluids.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Formulation 7:1 (228mg/5mL or 457mg/5mL). For Formulation 14:1, dose is 80-90 mg/kg/day.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Hospitalized / Toxic / Vomiting)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: First-line parenteral option. May add Amikacin if septic shock.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV / IM (Daily Inpatient / Outpatient Parenteral)
antibiotics.doseText: 75 - 100 mg/kg/day IV/IM in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once-daily dosing.

antibiotics.label: Amikacin IV (Add if septic or suspected resistant GNB)
antibiotics.doseText: 15 mg/kg/dose IV once daily (q24h) (max. 1.5g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Extended interval aminoglycoside dosing.

name: Lower Urinary Tract Infection (Acute Cystitis)
commonOrganisms: Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella pneumoniae
comments: Afebrile child with dysuria, frequency, or urgency. Short-course therapy is effective. Duration: 3 to 5 days.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1) (Preferred)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Standard 7:1 oral suspension.

antibiotics.label: Cefuroxime Axetil PO
antibiotics.doseText: 30 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 250mg/dose, 500mg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Take with food.

antibiotics.label: Co-trimoxazole (Bactrim) PO
antibiotics.doseText: 8 - 10 mg TMP/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses (max. 160mg TMP/dose, 320mg TMP/day)
antibiotics.notes: Contraindicated in severe G6PD deficiency and neonates.

antibiotics.label: Nitrofurantoin PO (Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 2 mg/kg/dose PO q12h (sustained-release) or 1 mg/kg/dose PO q6h (immediate-release) (max. 100mg/dose)
antibiotics.notes: For lower UTI only! Ineffective for pyelonephritis due to low tissue/renal parenchyma levels.

name: UTI Chemoprophylaxis (Recurrent UTI / High-Grade VUR)
commonOrganisms: Escherichia coli, Enterococcus, Klebsiella
comments: Indicated for recurrent febrile UTI or dilating vesicoureteral reflux (VUR Grade III-V) awaiting imaging/surgery. Give single bedtime dose.

antibiotics.label: Trimethoprim / Sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) PO (Bedtime Prophylaxis)
antibiotics.doseText: 2 mg TMP/kg/dose PO once daily at bedtime (max. 80mg TMP/dose)
antibiotics.notes: First choice for age > 6 weeks. Bedtime administration allows high urinary overnight concentration.

antibiotics.label: Nitrofurantoin PO (Bedtime Prophylaxis)
antibiotics.doseText: 1 - 2 mg/kg/dose PO once daily at bedtime (max. 100mg/dose)
antibiotics.notes: Contraindicated if CrCl < 30 mL/min, G6PD deficiency, or age < 1 month.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (Infants < 6 weeks / Neonates)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 - 15 mg/kg/dose PO once daily at bedtime (max. 250mg/dose)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred agent in young infants under 6 weeks where sulfonamides/nitrofurantoin are contraindicated.

name: Septic Arthritis & Acute Osteomyelitis
commonOrganisms: Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA/MRSA), Streptococcus pyogenes, S. pneumoniae, Kingella kingae (<5 yrs)
comments: Urgent surgical washout/aspiration indicated for septic arthritis. Total duration: Septic arthritis 3-4 weeks; Osteomyelitis 4-6 weeks. Switch to high-dose oral therapy (Cephalexin or Cloxacillin) once clinically improved, afebrile for 48h, and CRP declining by ≥50%.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (First-Line MSSA High-Dose)
antibiotics.doseText: 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 to 6 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 12g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Gold standard high-dose anti-staphylococcal therapy.

antibiotics.label: Cefazolin IV (Alternative First-Line - Convenient q8h)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 150 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 1g/dose, 4.5g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient 8-hourly dosing with lower incidence of phlebitis and hypersensitivity than cloxacillin.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Add if Age ≤ 3 months or Kingella suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Combine with Cloxacillin in infants ≤3 months for Gram-negative and GBS coverage.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Proven / Suspected MRSA)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Mandatory TDM. Maintain trough 15-20 mcg/mL for bone/joint penetration.

name: Acute Bacterial Meningitis (Infant & Child ≥3 months)
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae type b
comments: Medical emergency! Start empiric therapy immediately after blood culture. Do NOT delay antibiotics if lumbar puncture is postponed. Add Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg IV q6h before or with first dose for Hib/pneumococcal meningitis.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Preferred First Line Meningitic Dose)
antibiotics.doseText: 200 - 300 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 12g/day)
antibiotics.notes: High CNS penetration. Continue for minimum 10-14 days for S. pneumoniae, 7 days for N. meningitidis.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Meningitic Dose)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 mg/kg/day IV in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 4g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Can give as 100mg/kg OD or 50mg/kg q12h. Highly potent.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Combine if Cephalosporin-resistant Pneumococcus suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 60 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Add routinely if PRSP (penicillin/cephalosporin-resistant S. pneumoniae) is suspected.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (Add if Listeria monocytogenes suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 300 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 12g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Indicated in immunocompromised children or infants < 3 months.

name: Brain Abscess & Subdural Empyema
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus anginosus group, S. aureus, Enterobacterales, Anaerobes
comments: Urgent neurosurgical consultation for aspiration/drainage. Empiric therapy must cross blood-brain barrier and cover anaerobes. Duration: 4-6 weeks (longer if multiple non-drained lesions).

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV PLUS Metronidazole IV
antibiotics.doseText: Cefotaxime 200-300 mg/kg/day IV q6h + Metronidazole 30-40 mg/kg/day IV q8h
antibiotics.notes: Covers Streptococci, Gram-negative bacilli, and oral anaerobes.

antibiotics.label: Meropenem IV (Post-Neurosurgical / Hospital-Acquired / Pseudomonas)
antibiotics.doseText: 120 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: High meningitic doses with excellent anaerobic and Gram-negative penetration.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Add if Post-Craniotomy or MRSA suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: 60 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 15-20 mcg/mL.

name: Acute Bacterial Gastroenteritis / Dysentery (Bloody Diarrhoea)
commonOrganisms: Shigella spp., Salmonella (non-typhoidal), Campylobacter jejuni, E. histolytica
comments: Oral rehydration is paramount! Antibiotics are NOT routinely indicated for acute watery diarrhoea. Indicated only for macroscopic blood in stool (dysentery), systemic toxicity, severe malnutrition, or high-risk infants.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (First Line for Shigellosis & Campylobacter)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 - 12 mg/kg/day PO OD for 3 days (max. 500mg/day) OR 20 mg/kg single dose
antibiotics.notes: First choice in children. High intracellular tissue concentrations and short course.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Severe / Toxic / Sepsis / Unable to take oral)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 75 mg/kg/day IV once daily (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Parenteral therapy for children with severe dehydration, bacteraemia or vomiting.

antibiotics.label: Metronidazole PO (If Amoebic Dysentery / E. histolytica / Giardiasis)
antibiotics.doseText: 30 - 40 mg/kg/day PO in 3 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 1.5g/day)
antibiotics.notes: For trophozoites seen in stool microscopy or proven amoebic colitis.

name: Typhoid Fever / Enteric Fever
commonOrganisms: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, Salmonella Paratyphi
comments: High continuous fever, rose spots, hepatosplenomegaly, abdominal pain. Check blood culture, stool culture, and Widal/Tubex. Avoid premature discontinuation to prevent relapse.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (First-Line Inpatient)
antibiotics.doseText: 75 - 100 mg/kg/day IV once daily (max. 2g/day) for 10 to 14 days
antibiotics.notes: First-line parenteral therapy. Complete full 10-14 days.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (First-Line Oral - Uncomplicated)
antibiotics.doseText: 10 - 20 mg/kg/day PO once daily (max. 1g/day) for 7 days
antibiotics.notes: Excellent intracellular penetration and low relapse rate.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Alternative Parenteral)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Alternative 3rd generation cephalosporin.

name: Cholera (Vibrio cholerae)
commonOrganisms: Vibrio cholerae O1 / O139
comments: RAPID FLUID RESUSCITATION IS LIFE-SAVING! Antibiotics are an adjunct to rehydration to reduce stool volume and shorten vibrio excretion period.

antibiotics.label: Azithromycin PO (Single Dose - Preferred in Children)
antibiotics.doseText: 20 mg/kg PO as a single dose (max. 1g single dose)
antibiotics.notes: First line single-dose therapy endorsed by WHO and NAG 2024 for children.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO (Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 mg/kg/day PO in 4 divided doses (max. 1.6g/day) for 3 days
antibiotics.notes: Three-day regimen if azithromycin is unavailable.

name: Infective Endocarditis (IE - Native Valve / Empiric)
commonOrganisms: Viridans group Streptococci (40%), Staphylococcus aureus (35%), Enterococci, HACEK
comments: Obtain 3 sets of blood cultures from separate venipuncture sites before starting antibiotics. Urgent echocardiogram. Bactericidal synergistic combination required for 4-6 weeks.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV PLUS Gentamicin IV (Subacute / Community Native Valve)
antibiotics.doseText: Ampicillin 200-300 mg/kg/day IV q6h + Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV q8h
antibiotics.notes: Covers Viridans streptococci and Enterococcus with aminoglycoside synergy.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV PLUS Gentamicin IV (Acute / S. aureus Suspected)
antibiotics.doseText: Cloxacillin 200 mg/kg/day IV q6h + Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV q8h
antibiotics.notes: MSSA bactericidal regimen.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV PLUS Gentamicin IV (Prosthetic Valve / Hospital-Acquired / MRSA)
antibiotics.doseText: Vancomycin 45-60 mg/kg/day IV q6h + Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV q8h. Target trough 15-20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Add Rifampicin for prosthetic valve endocarditis.

name: Acute Bacterial / Purulent Pericarditis
commonOrganisms: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, H. influenzae, Gram-negative bacilli
comments: URGENT ECHOCARDIOGRAM! High risk of cardiac tamponade. Urgent pericardiocentesis / surgical drainage mandatory. Antibiotic duration: 4 weeks.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV PLUS Cefotaxime IV (First-Line Empiric)
antibiotics.doseText: Cloxacillin 200 mg/kg/day IV q6h (max. 12g) + Cefotaxime 200-300 mg/kg/day IV q6h (max. 12g)
antibiotics.notes: Covers MSSA, S. pneumoniae, and Gram-negative bacilli.

antibiotics.label: Cefazolin IV (Penicillin Allergy Alternative)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Non-severe allergy alternative.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (MRSA Suspected / Septic Shock)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 15-20 mcg/mL.

name: Acute Rheumatic Fever (ARF) - Secondary Chemoprophylaxis
ageSuitability: Children & Adolescents with prior ARF / RHD
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus)
comments: Continuous antimicrobial prophylaxis is vital to prevent recurrent GAS infections and progressive Rheumatic Heart Disease (RHD). Duration: Minimum 5-10 years post-attack or until age 21 (longer if significant residual valvular heart disease).

antibiotics.label: Benzathine Penicillin G (BPG) IM (Gold Standard Every 3-4 Weeks)
antibiotics.doseText: < 27 kg: 600,000 units IM every 3-4 weeks; ≥ 27 kg: 1,200,000 units (1.2 Mega units) IM every 3-4 weeks
antibiotics.notes: Most effective regimen to prevent recurrence. Deep IM injection.

antibiotics.label: Penicillin V (Phenoxymethylpenicillin) PO (Daily Oral Option)
antibiotics.doseText: 250 mg PO twice daily (q12h) continuously
antibiotics.notes: Oral alternative for patients refusing injections. Strict daily compliance required.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO (Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 250 mg PO twice daily (q12h) continuously
antibiotics.notes: For patients with documented penicillin allergy.

name: Post-Splenectomy / Functional Asplenia Chemoprophylaxis
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae (OPSS / overwhelming post-splenectomy sepsis), N. meningitidis, Hib
comments: Overwhelming Post-Splenectomy Sepsis (OPSS) carries a mortality rate >50%. Daily penicillin prophylaxis PLUS pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Hib vaccinations are lifesaving.

antibiotics.label: Penicillin V (Phenoxymethylpenicillin) PO
antibiotics.doseText: < 5 years: 125 mg PO q12h; ≥ 5 years: 250 mg PO q12h
antibiotics.duration: At least until age 5 (or minimum 2-3 years post-splenectomy)
antibiotics.notes: Continuous daily oral prophylaxis.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin PO (Alternative Daily Prophylaxis)
antibiotics.doseText: < 5 years: 125 mg PO once daily (OD); ≥ 5 years: 250 mg PO once daily (OD)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once-daily dosing.

antibiotics.label: Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate PO (Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: < 5 years: 125 mg PO q12h; ≥ 5 years: 250 mg PO q12h
antibiotics.notes: For patients with penicillin hypersensitivity.

name: Skin Abscess / Furuncle / Carbuncle
commonOrganisms: Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA / CA-MRSA)
comments: INCISION & DRAINAGE is primary definitive treatment! Antibiotics are indicated if: surrounding cellulitis > 2cm, systemic symptoms (fever, tachycardia), multiple abscesses, age < 6 months, or immunosuppression.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin PO/IV (First-Line MSSA)
antibiotics.doseText: Mild (PO): 50-100 mg/kg/day q6h (max. 2g/day); Severe (IV): 200 mg/kg/day q6h (max. 12g/day) for 5-7 days
antibiotics.notes: Take oral formulation 1 hour before food.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (First-Line Oral Alternative - Pleasant Taste)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 4 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day) for 5-7 days
antibiotics.notes: Excellent compliance in children.

antibiotics.label: Clindamycin PO (Suspected CA-MRSA / Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 20 - 30 mg/kg/day PO in 3 divided doses (max. 450mg/dose, 1.8g/day) for 5-7 days
antibiotics.notes: Covers MRSA and suppresses Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL) toxin production.

name: Skin & Soft Tissue: Impetigo / Erysipelas / Mild Cellulitis
commonOrganisms: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes (GAS)
comments: For localized non-bullous impetigo, crust removal and topical mupirocin 2% or fusidic acid is effective. If widespread, bullous impetigo, or cellulitis, start oral anti-staphylococcal therapy.

antibiotics.label: Cephalexin PO (First-Line Oral)
antibiotics.doseText: 25 - 50 mg/kg/day PO in 2 to 4 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day) for 5-7 days
antibiotics.notes: Pleasant suspension taste; superior adherence.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin PO (Oral Anti-Staphylococcal)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 - 100 mg/kg/day PO in 4 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 2g/day) 1 hour before food
antibiotics.notes: Must take on empty stomach.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Second-line for infected eczema or mixed wound infections.

antibiotics.label: Clindamycin PO (Severe Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: 20 - 30 mg/kg/day PO in 3 divided doses (max. 450mg/dose, 1.8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Alternative for beta-lactam allergic children.

name: Animal / Human Bite Wounds
commonOrganisms: Pasteurella multocida (cats/dogs), Eikenella corrodens (human), S. aureus, Anaerobes
comments: Copious wound irrigation with normal saline is mandatory. Do NOT suture puncture bite wounds! Tetanus prophylaxis assessment required.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1) (Drug of Choice)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin component) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day) for 5-7 days
antibiotics.notes: Gold standard bite coverage: covers Pasteurella, Eikenella, MSSA, and oral anaerobes.

antibiotics.label: Co-trimoxazole PO PLUS Metronidazole PO (Penicillin Allergy)
antibiotics.doseText: Cotrimoxazole 8-10 mg TMP/kg/day q12h + Metronidazole 30 mg/kg/day q8h for 5-7 days
antibiotics.notes: Pasteurella coverage with Cotrimoxazole plus anaerobic coverage with Metronidazole.

name: Neonatal Early-Onset Sepsis / Meningitis (≤ 7 days of life)
commonOrganisms: Group B Streptococcus (GBS), Escherichia coli, Listeria monocytogenes, Enterococcus
comments: Empiric combination therapy with Ampicillin + Aminoglycoside (Gentamicin) or Cefotaxime. Adjust Gentamicin dosing interval by gestational age (GA/CGA)!

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (Neonatal Sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 150 mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses (q12h if ≤7 days; if meningitis: 200-300 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses)
antibiotics.notes: For meningitis, increase to 200-300 mg/kg/day divided q12h (≤7 days) or q8h (>7 days).

antibiotics.label: Gentamicin IV (Neonatal Gestational-Age Regimen)
antibiotics.doseText: 5 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: <30w CGA: q48h; 30-34w CGA: q36h; ≥35w CGA: q24h
antibiotics.frequency: Stratified by Gestational Age (<30w: q48h, 30-34w: q36h, ≥35w: q24h)
antibiotics.notes: NAG 2024 CGA protocol. Monitor serum trough level (<1-2 mcg/mL) and peak level (5-10 mcg/mL).

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Alternative to Gentamicin or if Meningitis proven)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: ≤7 days PNA: q12h; >7 days PNA: q6h-q8h (max. 200mg/kg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Safe in neonates; does not displace bilirubin from albumin.

name: Neonatal Necrotising Enterocolitis (NEC - Stage 1 to 3)
commonOrganisms: Klebsiella spp., E. coli, Clostridia, CoNS, Enterococci, Bacteroides spp.
comments: Bowel rest, NPO, gastric decompression, fluid resuscitation and prompt triple broad-spectrum coverage.

antibiotics.label: Ampicillin IV (Stage 1 NEC)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: ≤1 week of age: q12h; >1 week of age: q8h
antibiotics.notes: Combine with Gentamicin + Metronidazole for Stage 1.

antibiotics.label: Gentamicin IV (NEC Stage 1)
antibiotics.doseText: 5 mg/kg/dose IV (<30w CGA: q48h; 30-34w CGA: q36h; ≥35w CGA: q24h)
antibiotics.notes: Can substitute with Amikacin 15mg/kg/dose if local Gram-negative resistance is high.

antibiotics.label: Metronidazole IV (Anaerobic Coverage for NEC)
antibiotics.doseText: Loading: 15 mg/kg IV once. Maintenance: ≤34w: 7.5 mg/kg q12h; 35-40w: 7.5 mg/kg q8h; >40w: 10 mg/kg q8h
antibiotics.notes: Crucial anaerobic gut flora coverage for bowel wall ischemia/necrosis.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (NEC Stage 2 / Stage 3 - In place of Amp+Gent)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/dose IV. Frequency: ≤1 week of age: q12h; >1 week of age: q8h (PLUS Metronidazole)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred for established pneumatosis intestinalis or perforation.

name: Febrile Neutropenia (Paediatric Oncology / Haematology)
commonOrganisms: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacteriaceae (Klebsiella, E. coli), Staphylococci, Streptococci
comments: MEDICAL EMERGENCY! Defined as single oral temp ≥ 38.3°C (or ≥ 38.0°C over 1 hour) with absolute neutrophil count (ANC) < 500/mm³. Administer broad-spectrum antipseudomonal monotherapy within 60 minutes of arrival.

antibiotics.label: Cefepime IV (First-Line Monotherapy)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/dose IV q8h (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Fourth generation cephalosporin with excellent Pseudomonas and Gram-negative coverage.

antibiotics.label: Piperacillin/Tazobactam IV (Tazocin) (Alternative First-Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 300 - 400 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 4.5g/dose, 16g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Provides broad anaerobic and antipseudomonal coverage.

antibiotics.label: Meropenem IV (Septic Shock / Persistent Fever / ESBL)
antibiotics.doseText: 60 - 120 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Step up for clinical deterioration, hemodynamic shock, or ESBL risk.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Add if Catheter Infection / Shock / Mucositis)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Do not add empiric vancomycin routinely unless specific high-risk criteria met (catheter exit-site infection, hemodynamic instability, severe mucositis).

name: Preseptal & Orbital Cellulitis
commonOrganisms: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, H. influenzae
comments: CRITICAL DISTINCTION: Orbital cellulitis involves proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, reduced vision, or pain with eye movement. Urgent contrast CT orbit/paranasal sinuses and emergency ENT/Ophthalmology review! Preseptal has normal visual acuity and painless ocular motility.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate PO (Augmentin 7:1) (Mild Preseptal Cellulitis Only)
antibiotics.doseText: 40 - 50 mg/kg/day (amoxicillin) PO in 2 divided doses (max. 2g/day) for 7-10 days
antibiotics.notes: Only for mild preseptal cellulitis in reliable family without orbital signs.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV PLUS Cloxacillin IV (Orbital / Severe Preseptal)
antibiotics.doseText: Cefotaxime 150-200 mg/kg/day IV q6h + Cloxacillin 100-200 mg/kg/day IV q6h (max. 8g each)
antibiotics.notes: Standard parenteral combination covering pneumococcus, H. influenzae, and MSSA.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Add if MRSA / Subperiosteal Abscess / Intracranial Spread)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 15-20 mcg/mL.

name: Melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei) (Updated Jan '26)
commonOrganisms: Burkholderia pseudomallei
comments: Two-phase therapy: Intensive IV phase (minimum 10-14 days; longer if deep organ abscesses or neuromelioidosis) followed by Eradication oral phase (minimum 12 weeks with Cotrimoxazole).

antibiotics.label: Ceftazidime IV (Intensive Phase - First Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Intensive phase. Infuse over 30-60 minutes.

antibiotics.label: Meropenem IV (Intensive Phase - Severe Sepsis / Neuromelioidosis)
antibiotics.doseText: 75 - 120 mg/kg/day IV in 3 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 6g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Preferred in septic shock or neuromelioidosis.

antibiotics.label: Co-trimoxazole (Bactrim) PO (Eradication Phase)
antibiotics.doseText: 8 - 10 mg TMP/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses with Folic Acid supplement (5mg/day)
antibiotics.notes: Eradication phase to prevent relapse. Co-prescribe Folic acid 5mg daily. Monitor FBC and renal profile.

name: Leptospirosis (Weil's Disease)
commonOrganisms: Leptospira interrogans
comments: History of freshwater exposure, flooding, or rodent contact. Biphasic illness (leptospiraemic phase then immune phase). Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction may occur within hours of antibiotic initiation.

antibiotics.label: Benzylpenicillin (Penicillin G) IV (Severe / Inpatient)
antibiotics.doseText: 200,000 - 400,000 units/kg/day IV in 4 to 6 divided doses (max. 24 million units/day) for 7 days
antibiotics.notes: First-line parenteral therapy for moderate to severe leptospirosis.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Parenteral)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 100 mg/kg/day IV once daily (max. 2g/day) for 7 days
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once-daily dosing with equal clinical efficacy.

antibiotics.label: Amoxicillin PO (Mild Leptospirosis)
antibiotics.doseText: 50 mg/kg/day PO in 3 divided doses (max. 500mg/dose, 1.5g/day) for 7 days
antibiotics.notes: For mild anicteric leptospirosis tolerating oral fluids.

name: Catheter-Related Bloodstream Infection (CRBSI)
ageSuitability: All paediatric ages with central line / PICC / Port-a-cath
commonOrganisms: CoNS (S. epidermidis), Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella, Enterobacter, Candida
comments: Take paired blood cultures: one from catheter hub and one from peripheral vein (differential time to positivity >2h indicates catheter source). Consider catheter removal for S. aureus, Candida, or refractory bacteremia.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (First-Line Empiric for CoNS & MRSA)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Mandatory TDM. Trough target 15-20 mcg/mL.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Add for Gram-Negative Bacilli Coverage)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Combine with Vancomycin for broad initial empiric coverage in sick children.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (Switch if MSCoNS or MSSA confirmed on blood culture)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: De-escalate from vancomycin once susceptibility confirms methicillin sensitivity.

name: Paediatric Sepsis & Septic Shock (Community-Acquired)
commonOrganisms: Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, Group A Streptococcus, Enterobacterales
comments: CRITICAL: Administer empiric intravenous antibiotics within the first hour of recognition ('Golden Hour'). Take blood cultures before starting antibiotics without delaying infusion.

antibiotics.label: Cefotaxime IV (Preferred First Line Sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 150 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Third-generation cephalosporin covering encapsulated organisms and GNB.

antibiotics.label: Ceftriaxone IV (Alternative Sepsis First Line)
antibiotics.doseText: 80 - 100 mg/kg/day IV in 1 to 2 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 4g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Convenient once or twice daily infusion. Avoid calcium co-administration.

antibiotics.label: Cloxacillin IV (Add for Staphylococcal toxic shock or purpura)
antibiotics.doseText: 100 - 200 mg/kg/day IV in 4 divided doses (max. 2g/dose, 8g/day)
antibiotics.notes: Add if staphylococcal sepsis or toxic shock syndrome suspected.

antibiotics.label: Gentamicin IV (Add for synergistic Gram-negative coverage in shock)
antibiotics.doseText: 7.5 mg/kg/dose IV once daily (q24h) (max. 400mg/day). Monitor trough level.
antibiotics.notes: Once daily extended interval dosing for synergy. Trough target < 1 mcg/mL.

antibiotics.label: Vancomycin IV (Add if MRSA risk or central line sepsis)
antibiotics.doseText: 45 - 60 mg/kg/day IV in 3 to 4 divided doses (max. 2g/day). Target trough 15 - 20 mcg/mL.
antibiotics.notes: Target trough: 15-20 mcg/mL.
